en.bestFor: Turning an idea, article or set of notes into a clear concept explainer for Reels, Shorts, marketing or presentations — any topic that is clearer as an explanation graph than as a character holding props.
en.structure: Each clip runs 3–8 seconds and the count follows the content: about 1–2 clips for a micro short, 2–4 for 15–20s, 4–6 for 30–45s, and 7–10 for a full 50–60s explainer.
en.hook: Clip 1 always opens with a punchy spoken line plus one exaggerated camera move, sharp and fast: a snap zoom in to a surprised face, a snap zoom out from the face to the full body, a fast 360 orbit around the character, an overhead drop onto the face, a crash push from far away into a close-up, or a dutch snap from a tilt into an upright view. Later clips do not repeat that move.
en.arc: Picks the pattern that suits the source, e.g. surprise → setup → how it works → consequence → takeaway for education, or pain point → reveal → proof → call to action for products. The main answer is held back until near the end, and the video finishes on a clean resting payoff rather than looping.
en.narrator: A warm adult male voice narrates every line from off-screen, in the third person. The character stays silent and never lip-syncs. With a character on screen, each clip is a new performance and does not repeat the last move or camera. Most clips keep them on one side with a bigger local move (a few steps, a jump, a walk toward or away from camera, a push or pull). Only occasionally do they cross the frame. The narrator may call them by name.
en.visual: A fixed whiteboard-doodle look: bold, slightly wobbly black lines with flat marker fills on a white canvas. Every topic is an explanation graph — comparison, before/after, cause and effect, steps, labeled parts, flow, or a chart — plus extra objects and doodles that explain the idea. With a character on screen, starting sides alternate and the camera changes (side, above, front, behind, toward, away). About 80% of clips stay on one side; about 20% cross left-to-right or right-to-left. Short beat titles and diagram labels sit on the canvas.
en.audio: Background music follows the emotional turn of the script, with quick sound effects (pops, whooshes, dings) timed to visual changes. Narration is voice only; beat titles and diagram labels may sit on the canvas.
en.rules: You must pick an aspect ratio. Keep the source's meaning and invent no facts. The explanation graph is the spine. With a character, do not walk left to right every clip. Alternate the starting side. About 80% of clips stay on that side (steps, a real jump, toward or away from camera, push or pull). Only about 20% cross left-to-right or right-to-left. Change the camera every clip. A jump lifts the feet; never slide upward. The last clip never points toward the camera. The whiteboard style and character stay locked. Approve the storyboard before any video.
